Changes since [1.4.0](https://github.com/ops-software/mini-oled-dock/releases/tag/v1.4.0): a reworked Start menu, the app's own jump list on right click, and pins that survive app updates.

### Fixes

- **Pinned apps keep working after the app updates itself.** Apps such as Discord install each version in its own folder (`app-1.0.9265`, then `app-1.0.9267`) and delete the old one. A pin kept the old path, so after an update its click did nothing and its icon was lost until you pinned the app again. The pin now follows the app: when the app is seen running from a newer folder, or the stored file is gone and a newer folder holds it, the dock uses the new path and saves it in `config.json`. Only the version folder is ever changed; a launch target you set by hand is left alone.
- **Popups follow the Opacity slider.** The Start menu, Audio, Calendar and the other popups now use the bar's opacity instead of a fixed one. With the default 95 % nothing visibly changes.

### App menu

- **The app's jump list on right click.** The right-click menu of an app in the bar now shows what the app itself offers in the Windows taskbar, above the dock's own rows (New window, Pin / Unpin, Close): its tasks (Steam's Store / Library / Friends, "New window" of VS Code, the profiles of Windows Terminal) and its own categories (recently played games, recent folders). A click starts the entry with normal user rights.
- **Limits.** Up to 9 tasks and 5 entries of the other categories are shown. The lists Windows keeps by itself (Recent and Frequent files) are not shown, entries have no icons, and an entry whose name is a resource reference is skipped.
- **How it is read.** The dock runs as administrator and the jump list files can be written by any program of the user, so they are treated as untrusted: the dock reads them with its own parser, never hands them to the Windows shortcut loader, loads no icon from them, and starts an entry only when you click it, through Explorer and never elevated.

### Start menu

- **Search with Windows' own data.** The search uses the synonyms and the popularity ranks Windows ships ("rdp" finds Remote Desktop Connection), its typo corrections when nothing matches, and the catalog of the Settings app and the Control Panel, so settings can be found and opened from the menu. Apps always rank above settings.
- **Right click on an app:** pin / unpin, remove from folder, run as administrator, open file location, uninstall (opens Installed apps). "Run as administrator" now works for any app of the menu: Explorer shows the UAC prompt, the dock's own rights are never used.
- **Folders.** In the Windows 11 layout, drag a pinned app onto another one to make a folder, onto a folder to add it, out of an open folder to take it out. Click a folder's name to rename it. Dragging to the side of a pin reorders.
- **Letter jump** in All apps.
- **Layouts renamed and redone.** Vertical and Horizontal are now **Compact** (a launcher: one strip of pinned icons, the A-Z list below) and **Windows 11** (one scrolling page with the pinned tiles and All apps, a Grid / List switch, the user name and shortcuts to Settings, Explorer, Documents and Downloads). Old values in `config.json` are still read.
- **The power button is no longer in the Start menu:** the bar always has the power module.
- **App names in the bar are localized** like in the Windows Start menu (for example "Connessione Desktop remoto").
- **Memory.** The search data is loaded when the menu opens and freed, with the icons, 60 s after it closes.

### Start button menu

- **Terminal** (normal rights) replaces **PowerShell (admin)**. Terminal (admin) stays.

### Known issues

- A Start menu folder can be left with a single app in it.

### Install / update

Requires Windows 11. From 1.4.0 the dock finds this release by itself: an orange dot shows on **Settings** in the power popup, and **Settings → Updates → Update now** installs it. Or download `dock.exe` and run it from a terminal:

```powershell
.\dock.exe --install
```

It asks for administrator rights, copies itself to `%ProgramFiles%\mini-oled-dock` and starts with Windows. Settings are kept.
